declarations.name: defineShellWidgets
declarations.description:
Registers every element connectShell draws, under its default name: the widgets the documents,
the folder and a project are shown in, the shell's parts, the modules' views, the shell's
internal elements, and `<dex-app-shell>` with its views and actions. Call it once before
connectShell; a second call does nothing.

The shell's About popover, opened from the (i) button of an activity bar: a heading (the app's
name) and the lines the app hands it, each a label and its value (the app's version, the
versions it is built on). The app's words are drawn as text, never as markup.

show() opens it beside the button that opened it, as `<dex-settings-panel>` opens; Escape, a
press outside it, or close() closes it, and focus goes back to the button. It sends nothing.
declarations.name: DexAboutPanel

Opens the popover beside `anchor`, the button that opened it, in viewport px (its
getBoundingClientRect()): to its right with their bottoms in line, or to its left when the

not open.

members.name: close
members.description: Closes the popover; focus goes back to the button when the popover held it.

attributes.name: heading
attributes.description: The heading, the app's name, drawn in capitals as the Settings title is; also the dialog's accessible name.

declarations.name: defineAboutPanel
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-about-panel>`, or under `tag`.

The frame of an app: a toolbar and a location bar across the top, a
sidebar on each side with an activity bar beyond it, the documents in the center with a bottom
panel under them, and a status bar at the foot of the center. The page fills it: its toolbar,
location bar and status text as children in the `toolbar`, `location` and `status` slots, its
documents as plain children, and the sides from `<dex-shell-view>` children, each a view with
an activity button, and `<dex-shell-action>` children, buttons it answers itself.

Each side shows one of its views and hides the rest. A press of a view's activity button, its
shortcut, or toggleView shows the view, or closes its side when the view is the one shown; a
view its shortcut shows takes the focus, and the focus in a view that is hidden goes to the
view's button. A side's separator resizes it, dragged or by the arrow keys, and every side is
drawn no larger than the window leaves room for. A side with no views has no sidebar, and an
activity bar only for its actions. A change of the view shown, or of a side open or closed,
sends `dex-shell-view-changed`; a press of an action sends `dex-shell-action`. With a
`storage-key` the layout the person chose is kept in localStorage and read back by the next
shell with that key.
declarations.name: DexAppShell

members.name: storageKey
members.description:
The localStorage key the layout is kept under (which view each side shows, which sides are
open, and their sizes), read back as each side's views first arrive. Empty, the default,
keeps nothing. Attribute `storage-key`.

members.name: mono
members.description:
Draws the icons of the buttons the shell draws (the activity bars' and the status bar's) in
one colour, the buttons' ink (`--dex-activity-fg`, through `<dex-icon mono>`), as the
prototype's bars drew their glyphs; off, the default, draws them in their files' colours. The
page's own children are its own to draw. Attribute `mono`, reflected so a page's stylesheet
can follow it.

members.name: layout
members.description:
Which view each side shows, whether it is open, and its width or height, as drawn. A size the
window has no room for is drawn smaller than the one the person chose, and as chosen again
once there is room; the size kept is the one chosen. Read-only: the buttons, the separators,
showView and toggleView change it.

members.name: showView
members.description:
Shows the view with this id, opening its side if it was closed: what a command that brings a
view forward does. Never closes a side. Sends `dex-shell-view-changed`, and keeps the layout,
when that changes anything. A view appended in the same task is one too; an id no view has
does nothing.

members.name: toggleView
members.description:
What a press of the view's activity button does: shows it, or closes its side when it is the
view shown. Sends `dex-shell-view-changed` and keeps the layout. An id no view has does nothing.

members.name: anchorOf
members.description:
The box of the activity button of the view or the action with this id, in viewport px, for a
popover to open against; null when the shell draws no button for the id.

events.name: dex-shell-view-changed
events.description:
A side shows another view, or was opened or closed: by its activity button, its chord, or
showView / toggleView. The side as it is now. Not sent for a resize, nor when the page's own
change of the views moves the layout.

events.name: dex-shell-action
events.description: An action's button, or its chord, was pressed: open what it stands for, against `anchor`.

attributes.name: storage-key
attributes.description:
The localStorage key the layout is kept under (which view each side shows, which sides are
open, and their sizes), read back as each side's views first arrive. Empty, the default,
keeps nothing. Attribute `storage-key`.

attributes.name: mono
attributes.description:
Draws the icons of the buttons the shell draws (the activity bars' and the status bar's) in
one colour, the buttons' ink (`--dex-activity-fg`, through `<dex-icon mono>`), as the
prototype's bars drew their glyphs; off, the default, draws them in their files' colours. The
page's own children are its own to draw. Attribute `mono`, reflected so a page's stylesheet
can follow it.

cssProperties.name: --dex-bg-activity-bar
cssProperties.description: The app shell (data-explorer-view/app-shell): its activity bars, toolbar row, tab bar and the line a resizer shows under the pointer.

declarations.name: defineAppShell
declarations.description:
Registers the widget as `<dex-app-shell>`, or under `tag`, and the parts it is given and draws:
`<dex-shell-view>`, `<dex-shell-action>` and `<dex-icon>`. The parts first, so the views of a
page are upgraded before the shell reads them. The layout's alone: what connectShell builds in it
is defined, this with it, by defineShellWidgets().

A question with buttons, asked in the page for a host that has no dialogs of its own (a
browser page): "Save changes to x before closing?", "x changed on disk". show() opens it and
resolves to the id of the button pressed; Escape, a click outside it and close() resolve to the
question's `cancelId`, and focus goes back where it was. It opens focused on the primary
button, never on a danger one, and Tab stays among its buttons while it is open. It sends no
events: the promise is the answer.

It paints at z-index 10000, as `<dex-error-dialog>` does, so where both are open the one later
in the document is on top: append it last in the body, outside any element that makes a
stacking context of its own.
declarations.name: DexConfirmDialog

members.name: show
members.description:
Opens the dialog with `options` and resolves to the id of the button pressed, or to
`options.cancelId` on Escape, a click on the backdrop, close(), or the element leaving the
page. A second show() while one is open answers the first with the first's `cancelId` and
asks the second in its place. Focus opens on the first primary button, or with none on the
first that is not a danger one, and returns, when the dialog closes, to the element that had
it when the first of these questions was asked. On an element that is not on the page it
resolves to `cancelId` at once.

members.name: close
members.description: Closes the dialog, answering show() with its `cancelId`; does nothing while closed.

declarations.name: defineConfirmDialog
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-confirm-dialog>`, or under `tag`.

The row of tabs above an app's documents, one per open file, as `tabs` lists them, `active`
marking the one shown. It draws them and asks for everything else: a click (or Enter or Space)
sends `dex-tab-select`, × (or a middle click, Delete or Backspace) `dex-tab-close`, a double-click
`dex-tab-pin`, and a tab dropped on another `dex-tab-move`. Which tabs there are, in what
order, and which is active stay the app's: nothing here changes `tabs` or `active`.

A preview tab's label is italic; an unsaved one shows ● where its × is, until the pointer or the
keyboard comes onto it. A row too long for its width scrolls sideways (a wheel scrolls it too),
keeps the active tab in view, and offers a … button listing every tab. The arrow keys move the
focus along the tabs, and Home and End to either end.
declarations.name: DexDocTabs

members.name: tabs
members.description: The tabs, in order: plain data, which the app replaces as files open, close and move. Default none.

members.name: active
members.description: The id of the tab shown, which is marked selected and scrolled into view. Default none. Attribute `active`.

events.name: dex-tab-select
events.description: Show this tab: a click on it, Enter or Space on it, or its item in the … menu. Sent for the active tab too.

events.name: dex-tab-close
events.description: Close this tab: its ×, a middle click on it, or Delete (or Backspace) on it.

events.name: dex-tab-pin
events.description:
Keep this tab, no longer a preview: a double-click on it, whether it is a preview or not. Its
two clicks have each sent `dex-tab-select` first.

events.name: dex-tab-move
events.description: Move this tab: it was dropped on the tab at `index`. Remove it from `tabs`, then insert it at `index`.

attributes.name: active
attributes.description: The id of the tab shown, which is marked selected and scrolled into view. Default none. Attribute `active`.

cssProperties.name: --dex-color-modified
cssProperties.description: The Status column's "Modified".

declarations.name: defineDocTabs
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-doc-tabs>`, or under `tag`, and the `<dex-icon>` its tabs draw.

The open files, as the app shell's Explorer lists them: Root first, then each kind of file
under a heading of its own (Simulink Models, Data Dictionaries, MAT-Files, Projects, Other,
always in that order, and a heading only over files), each file with a twisty that opens it
onto its sections.

It draws what it is given and asks for the rest. A click on a row sends `dex-explorer-open`
for it, unpinned; a double-click or Enter sends it pinned; a right-click on a file sends
`dex-explorer-menu`. Which file a row is, what opening it means and which row is the current
one are the app's: the row `selected` names is highlighted, and a click changes nothing of it.
Which files are open in the tree (their twisty) is the element's own, but for one thing: a
`selected` that moves to a section of a closed file opens that file, at once or as soon as the
file lists the section, and the row `selected` moves to is scrolled into view. A file that
leaves `files` is forgotten, so it comes back closed, and a focused row that leaves passes the
focus to the next row.

The arrow keys walk the rows (the headings are no rows): Right opens a file or goes into it,
Left closes it or goes from a section to its file, Home and End go to the first and the last.
declarations.name: DexExplorer

members.name: files
members.description:
The open files, in the order each heading lists them. Replacing them keeps open each file
still here (by its `id`) and forgets the rest. Default none: Root alone.

members.name: selected
members.description:
The row to highlight: Root, a file, or a section of a file. Null, the default, highlights
none. The app sets it; the element never changes it, and setting it sends nothing. Moved to
another row, it scrolls that row into view once it is drawn; moved to a section of a closed
file, it opens the file, then or once a later `files` lists the section. The user may close
it again, and it stays closed until `selected` next moves to one of its sections.

members.name: rootLabel
members.description: What the first row, the one for every open file at once, reads. Default `Root`. Attribute `root-label`.

events.name: dex-explorer-open
events.description:
Open this row: Root, a file or a section. Unpinned for a click, pinned for a double-click or
Enter. A request: the explorer changes nothing itself, not even `selected`.

events.name: dex-explorer-menu
events.description: Show this file's menu at this point of the viewport: a file's row was right-clicked. A request.

attributes.name: root-label
attributes.description: What the first row, the one for every open file at once, reads. Default `Root`. Attribute `root-label`.

cssProperties.name: --dex-selection-fg
cssProperties.description: The ink on a selected row, whose surface is --dex-color-accent-bg.

declarations.name: defineExplorer
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-explorer>`, or under `tag`, and the `<dex-icon>` its rows draw.

The location bar: Back, Forward and Up, then a breadcrumb of where the user is, one segment
for each place on the way down to it ("Root › dd.sldd › Design Data"). It draws the segments
it is given, the last one as the current place, and turns each press into a request,
`dex-location-go`; it keeps no history and works out no path, so the app decides what each
request does, and says by `canBack`, `canForward` and `canUp` which buttons can be used. A
path too long for the bar shrinks its segments, each label ending in an ellipsis.
declarations.name: DexLocationBar

members.name: segments
members.description: The places on the way to where the user is, the first at the top and the last the current place. Default none.

members.name: canBack
members.description: Back can be used: there is a place to go back to. Off, the default, disables it. Attribute `can-back`.

members.name: canForward
members.description: Forward can be used: the user went back, and can go forward again. Off, the default, disables it. Attribute `can-forward`.

members.name: canUp
members.description: Up can be used: the current place is inside another one. Off, the default, disables it. Attribute `can-up`.

members.name: mono

Draws the icons of Back, Forward and Up in one colour, the text's (`<dex-icon mono>`), as a
toolbar's glyphs; off, the default, draws them in their files' colours. A segment's icon is a
file's or an entry's kind, which its colours tell apart, and keeps them either way. Attribute
`mono`, reflected so a page's stylesheet can follow it.

events.name: dex-location-go
events.description:
The user asked to move: Back, Forward or Up was pressed (only while `canBack`, `canForward`
or `canUp` says it can be), or a segment was, the last one included. The bar changes nothing
itself; the app moves, and gives it the new segments.

The shell's Settings popover, opened from the gear of an activity bar: the theme (Auto, Light,
Dark, Hi-Con), the toolbar's density (Normal, Compact: smaller icons with the labels beside
them), the icons of the shell's buttons (Minimal, in one colour, or Colorful) and the tables'
rules (Grid or Rows), each a row of segments that is a radio group. It shows `settings` and asks
for a change: a click, or an arrow key inside a group, sends `dex-settings-change` with the whole
new record and changes nothing by itself. The app applies the settings, keeps them, and sets
`settings` back; the popover stays open, so the themes can be tried one after another.

show() opens it beside the button that opened it (placeBeside, in data-explorer-view/model),
focused on the chosen theme; Escape, a press outside it, or close() closes it, and focus goes
back to the button.
declarations.name: DexSettingsPanel

members.name: settings
members.description:
The settings shown: which segment of each row is checked. The app sets it, at first and
after each `dex-settings-change` it applies; the panel never changes it itself.

Opens the popover beside `anchor`, the button that opened it, in viewport px (its

right has no room, and inside the window. Focus goes to the chosen theme. Open already, it
moves; not on the page, it does not open.

A segment other than the checked one was chosen, by a click or an arrow key: apply these
settings, keep them, and set `settings` to them. The popover stays open.

One view of the app shell: what the page shows in one of its sides (the left or the right
sidebar, or the bottom panel), and what the shell needs to give it an activity button. Its
children are the view's content; it is a column as wide and as tall as the side it is in, and
scrolls what does not fit.

The shell draws the view's button (its `icon`, with `label` and `shortcut` as the tooltip), in
the order the views are in the page, shows the view when the button is pressed, and heads the
side with its label. A view the side does not show is `hidden`, and stays in the page, so its
content keeps its state (a scroll position, a tree's open rows) for when it is shown again. The
view puts itself in the shell's slot for its side: a page writes only `side`. Shown by its
shortcut, it takes the focus: its first control, or itself when it has none (it takes the focus
from a script, and is no stop for Tab).
declarations.name: DexShellView

members.name: side
members.description: The side the view is on: `left`, `right` or `bottom`. Default `left`. Attribute `side`.

members.name: view
members.description:
The view's id, which the shell's `showView`, `toggleView` and `anchorOf` take, its events name
and its kept layout holds. One view per id: a second view with an id already given is drawn
nowhere. A view without one is not drawn. Attribute `view`.

members.name: label
members.description: What the view is called: its button's tooltip and accessible name, and its side's header. Attribute `label`.

members.name: icon
members.description: The id of the icon its activity button draws (`<dex-icon>`'s `iconId`). Attribute `icon`.

members.name: shortcut
members.description:
The keyboard chord that shows the view, or closes its side when it is shown, as a press of its
button does, written as the shell's chords are (`Mod+Shift+E`: Mod is Command on macOS and
Ctrl elsewhere). Its tooltip names it in the platform's words. Text that is not a chord is no
shortcut, and the tooltip then names none. A chord with no Mod, Ctrl or Alt (a bare key, or
Shift and a key) works in a text field too, where the key would type: the shell hears the
press on the window, and only a field that prevents its default keeps it. Default none.
Attribute `shortcut`.

attributes.description: The side the view is on: `left`, `right` or `bottom`. Default `left`. Attribute `side`.

and its kept layout holds. One view per id: a second view with an id already given is drawn
nowhere. A view without one is not drawn. Attribute `view`.

shortcut, and the tooltip then names none. A chord with no Mod, Ctrl or Alt (a bare key, or

The shell's toasts, in the bottom-right corner of the window: show() adds one at the bottom
of the stack. A 'status' or 'info' toast goes by itself after its `ms`; a 'warning' or an
'error' stays until its × is pressed, since what it says has to be read. A toast the pointer
is on, or whose × has focus, waits for the user, and is timed afresh once they leave it. At
most three are shown, and a fourth takes the oldest away. A screen reader hears each one as it
is shown, politely for 'status' and 'info' and at once for 'warning' and 'error'. It sends no
events: what it shows is the app's business, and closing one changes nothing but the screen.

members.description:

(default 4000); 'warning' and 'error' stay until closed, whatever `ms` says. At most three
are shown: a fourth takes the oldest away.

members.name: clear
members.description: Takes every toast away, stops every timer, and empties what a screen reader would read.

declarations.name: defineToastHost
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-toast-host>`, or under `tag`.

A row of buttons, the items an app hands it: each an icon over a small label (beside it with
`compact`, and in the label's colour with `mono`), the items of a group together with a separator
between groups, and the `end` items pushed to the right. A click on an item that is not disabled
sends `dex-toolbar-action` with its id; a disabled item is greyed and sends nothing. Each item's
tooltip is its `title`, or its label and shortcut.

The toolbar is one tab stop: the arrow keys move along the items, disabled ones included, and
wrap at either end; Home and End go to the first and the last; Enter and Space press the one the
keyboard is on. A mouse press takes no focus: it stays where the user was working. So an edit
open in a table's cell stays open too (the table commits one as its editor loses the focus), and
the app commits it, with connectTable's `handle.commitEdit()`, before it acts on
`dex-toolbar-action`. The toolbar knows nothing of files or tables: the app gives it new `items`
as what they can do changes, and does what `dex-toolbar-action` asks.

edge, each side in the order given. Replace the array to change them; an item keeps its
button, and the keyboard's place on it, while its `id` stays, and an item that goes while the
keyboard is on it hands the focus to the one that takes its place. Default none.

item's icon is greyed with its label either way. Attribute `mono`, reflected so a page's
stylesheet can follow it.

listens on the document tells a toolbar press from a menu choice.

The shell's command palette: a box at the top of the window, over the page, in which a few
typed letters find a command. show() opens it with the commands to offer; the list follows
the typing, labels that begin with the query first, then those whose words it begins, then
those that merely hold its letters in order (the letters matched are drawn in bold), and the
commands run lately come first among equals and first of all before anything is typed.
ArrowUp and ArrowDown move the active row, wrapping; Enter or a click runs it, which closes
the palette and sends `dex-palette-run`. A disabled command is greyed and runs on neither, and
the list opens on the first that can run. Escape, a click outside it and close() close it,
sending nothing.

It is a modal, as `<dex-confirm-dialog>` is: while it is open Tab stays in its input, no key
pressed in it reaches the page, a press in it keeps the focus in its input, and Escape is heard
wherever the focus is, but for a key pressed in another modal opened over it (an element with
`aria-modal="true"`, such as a confirm dialog a command asked), which is that modal's. When it
closes the focus goes back where it was, before `dex-palette-run` is sent, so a command that
moves the focus itself (showing the Explorer) keeps it there. It paints at z-index 10000, as
the dialogs do: append it last in the body, outside any element that makes a stacking context
of its own.

arrive, until the user scrolls up to read an older one; scrolled back to the bottom, it

How the open models, dictionaries and MAT-files connect: the models on the left as a tree of
their references, the data files on the right, each a box of its kind's colour, a file referenced
and not open dashed, and the edges between them. Every box starts closed. An open box lists the
blocks and variables that take part, a model's workspace variables under a divider, and every
other box the items of its own those reach (a model open shows, in a dictionary, the variables
its blocks read), with an edge from each block to each variable it reads, labelled with the block
parameter. The edges run under the boxes; what the selection reaches is drawn over them. The
graph comes from `buildRelationshipGraph`; where it is drawn, from `layoutGraph`.

A click on a box or an item selects it (`dex-graph-selected`), and lights it and what its edges
reach, dimming the rest; a click on the background clears it. A double-click asks to open the
file (`dex-graph-open`), at the item's row for an item, and a ghost by the reference that names
it, for the app to look for. A box's − or + asks to hide or show its
items (`dex-graph-expand`); the app answers by setting `expanded`. A box so opened is zoomed to
with the files it reaches, the rest dimmed, as the prototype's expand did, until it is closed,
Escape is pressed or the background clicked; a double-click on the background asks to close
every box and fits the graph. The pointer on an item traces what it is joined to, as a selection
of it would; on an edge, it fades the others. The wheel, the + and − buttons and a drag of the
background zoom and pan; the fit button and fit() show the whole graph, reveal() brings one box
or item to the middle, and zoomToReach() one and what it reaches. A Legend, closed at first,
names the kinds.

The keyboard: the canvas is one stop of the tab order; the arrows move the selection to the
nearest box that way, Enter opens the selected box or item, Space shows or hides the selected
box's items, Escape clears the selection and the dimming of a box opened, + and − zoom and 0
fits.

members.name: graph
members.description:

draws a note saying what to open. A new graph whose boxes are other than the last one's is

members.name: selected
members.description:
The id of the box or item to select: a box's id (a file's uri, for a file given) or an item's,
as `graphIdOf` gives it. It is lit with what its edges reach, and the rest is dimmed. Null, the
default, selects nothing. A click changes it and sends `dex-graph-selected`; setting it sends
nothing. Attribute `selected`.

members.name: expanded
members.description:
The ids of the boxes that are open. An open box shows all its items, and each other box the
items of its own an open box's edges reach: a model open shows its blocks and, in each data file
they read, only the variables they read. None, the default, the graph starts with: the files
and the links between them. The app sets it, in answer to `dex-graph-expand`; the element never
changes it.

members.name: layout
members.description:
How the graph is laid out. 'tree', the default, is the prototype's: two columns of top-down
trees, what a file references side by side in the row under it. 'indented' draws each column
as a file tree, one box a row, what a file references in the rows under it a step to the right,
which draws a large set of files narrower and so at a larger scale: fifteen files that fit a
1440 by 900 window's shell at 0.7 in trees fit it at 1.0 indented. A long indented column is
dealt into columns side by side for a fixed 900 by 600 canvas, not for the element's size. A
change fits the graph afresh, its boxes being elsewhere; what is open and selected stays. A
value it does not know is 'tree'. Attribute `layout`.

members.name: fit
members.description:
Scales and moves the view so the whole graph shows, centred, at no more than its own size and
no less than 0.7 of it: a graph bigger than that shows from its top left, to pan from.
Called with a draw to come (just after `graph` or `expanded` was set), it fits what that draw
lays out; before the element has a size (not on the page yet, or hidden), once it has one.

members.name: reveal
members.description:
Moves the view so the box or item `id` is at the middle of the canvas, at the scale it has; an
item of a closed box brings its box. Changes neither the selection nor which boxes are open:
an app revealing a row sets `selected` (and `expanded`) too, and may call this straight after,
since with a draw to come it reveals where that draw puts the row. An id the graph does not
hold moves nothing.

members.name: zoomToReach
members.description:
Zooms the view onto the box or item `id` and what a selection of it lights (it, what its edges
reach, and their boxes), centred, at no more than their own size and no less than the least a
fit shrinks to; where they do not fit at that, the box or item itself is kept in view, its top
left first. For an app's "Show in Graph", which sets `selected` (and `expanded`) too and may call
this straight after: with a draw to come, it zooms onto where that draw puts them. Changes
neither the selection nor which boxes are open; an id the graph does not hold moves nothing.

declarations.default: css` :host { display: block; position: relative; overflow: hidden; width: 100%; height: 100%; min-height: 120px; background: var(--dex-bg-tertiary, #f5f5f5); font-family: var(--dex-font-family, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif); color: var(--dex-color-text, #333); } /* The canvas is the whole host; the world inside it is the graph at its own size, moved and scaled by the view. */ .canvas { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; outline: none; cursor: grab; touch-action: none; } .canvas.panning { cursor: grabbing; } .canvas:focus-visible { box-shadow: inset var(--dex-focus-ring, 0 0 0 2px rgba(0, 120, 212, 0.4)); } .empty { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 16px; text-align: center; font-size: var(--dex-font-size, 13px); color: var(--dex-color-text-muted, #666); cursor: default; } .world { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; transform-origin: 0 0; } svg.edges { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; overflow: visible; pointer-events: none; } /* Two classes, so no colour rule of a kind (which fills the markers too, and a data link's has two classes of its own) fills a route. */ .edges path.edge { fill: none; stroke-width: 1.5; transition: opacity 0.15s ease, stroke-width 0.15s ease; } /* The edges under the boxes take the pointer, so one can be picked out by hovering it. The ones over the boxes never do: they would take the clicks meant for the items under them. */ .under path.edge { stroke-width: 1.2; opacity: 0.8; pointer-events: stroke; } .under path.edge:hover { stroke-width: 2.5; opacity: 1; } /* While an edge is under the pointer the others fade, as the prototype faded them, so the one picked out can be followed across the graph: every other edge under the boxes, and what is drawn over them. One dimmed already stays as dim. */ .world.edge-hover .under path.edge:not(:hover):not(.dim), .world.edge-hover .over > :not(.dim) { opacity: 0.3; } .over path.edge, path.stub { stroke-width: 1.8; } .edges path.stub { fill: none; } path.edge.dim, path.stub.dim { opacity: 0.2; } .model-ref { stroke: var(--dex-graph-edge-model-ref, #6788a4); fill: var(--dex-graph-edge-model-ref, #6788a4); } .sldd-ref { stroke: var(--dex-graph-edge-sldd-ref, #658d72); fill: var(--dex-graph-edge-sldd-ref, #658d72); } .data-link { stroke: var(--dex-graph-edge-data-link, #7c8a60); fill: var(--dex-graph-edge-data-link, #7c8a60); } /* A data link in the colour of the file it links, as the prototype drew them: no token of its own, the border's of a box of that kind, which is 3:1 against the canvas in every theme. */ .data-link.to-sldd { stroke: var(--dex-graph-sldd-border, #6a8c7a); A folder's hierarchy as a tree: each project and folder, the files in it, and under each file
the files it references, opened a level at a time. The rows are HierarchyItems
(`data-explorer-view/model`'s FolderHierarchy makes them); the rows under one are asked of

file's name and kind, an unresolved reference a warning, a file's mark a badge (a circular
reference, unsaved changes), and a notice (a folder of which only the first files are shown) an
information mark.

A click or Enter chooses a row: it is selected, `dex-hierarchy-selected` says which file it
opens, and a row with rows under it opens or closes. The arrow keys move through the rows
(Right opens a row or goes into it, Left closes it or goes to its parent), Home and End go to
the first and the last. `revealRow` shows a row the app names (the file it has open), and
`expandTopLevel` opens the folder's own row on first show. connectHierarchy wires one to a
FolderHierarchy.

declarations.name: esc
declarations.description:
Everything that reaches the markup, escaped — the page's single rule.

Numbers are accepted, not just strings, so a count is escaped by the same call as
the name beside it. Counts look exempt — a count is declared a number, and a number
cannot carry a `<` — but that type is a claim core's parser makes, and this
page sits on the far side of a postMessage boundary, where the payload is JSON and
nothing re-checks the declaration. While this took `string` only, a count could not
use it and was concatenated bare instead; `memberCount` then rendered escaped in the
identity block and raw in the Labels header, one field under two rules, and the
second was the wrong one (CodeQL js/xss, 2026-10-01).

`null` is NOT in the parameter type and must not be added. `memberCount` and friends are
nullable for a format that records no member list, and this signature is what turns one
of them reaching the markup into a compile error at the call site instead of the word
'null' on a customer's page — core's ProjectPage.memberCount relies on that by name.
Widening here, or defaulting the argument, moves the decision out of the renderer that
has to make it (see labelsSection).

`'` is deliberately absent: every attribute written here is double-quoted, and the
test that pins that is the reminder to keep it so.

declarations.name: filterTerms
declarations.description:
Split a filter query into terms.

Bare terms only: whitespace-separated, case-insensitive substring, ANDed. This is
deliberately NOT the table's `rowFilter.ts` grammar, which is column-aware
(`Name:foo`, comparison operators) and needs each row to be a record of named
columns. A page section is not a table — Project Path rows have one field, Labels
are chips and are not filtered at all — so adopting that grammar would mean
inventing column names per section to expose a syntax nobody asked for. What IS
shared is the part a user actually types: several words, all of which must appear.

declarations.name: highlight
declarations.description:
Escaped `text` with every occurrence of every term wrapped in `<mark>`.

Overlapping and adjacent hits are merged before wrapping. Two terms that overlap
in one word (`sup` and `upp` in "support") would otherwise emit nested or
interleaved marks, i.e. broken markup, from input the user typed by accident.

handle that says what the app is to do (`on`), and through which it selects.

(or per class a MAT-file takes), grouped by section. A click on a tile sends `dex-add-tile`;
the table turns it into `dex-add-entry`. Its Keep open box pins it open across adds

`dex-row-selected`; setting it sends nothing. Default none. Property only.

members.name: tableStyle
members.description:
`normal`, the default, rules every cell; `light` drops the lines between columns and keeps a
faint one between rows. Reflected to the attribute `table-style`.

members.name: columnLabels
members.description:
Each column's header text, by column key (`{ DataType: 'Data Type' }`), also the name a
search may qualify a term with (`"Data Type":double`); a column with none shows its key.
Default null. Property only.

members.name: columnGroups
members.description:
The group heading each column sits under in the Columns menu, by column key. Default null:
no headings. Property only.

members.name: columns
members.description:
The column keys this document has, which the Columns menu offers; the user's saved order and
choice of hidden ones apply within them. Default null: the built-in set. Property only.

members.name: banners
members.description:
The banners drawn above the search bar: an error, a notice, and what the document's read
could not read (TableBanners), each when present. connectTable sets it from what its source
says. Default null: none. Property only.

members.name: loading
members.description:
The rows are on their way: while there are none, the table says Loading… (with a spinner,
after half a second) instead of "No data"; the search bar stays. Set it while a document is
read. Default false. Attribute `loading`.

members.name: canAdd
members.description:
Whether this view can create entries, i.e. whether the `+ Add` button (and its gallery,
whose tiles send `dex-add-entry`) exists at all. Default false. Attribute `can-add`.

members.name: addClasses
members.description:
The classes a MAT-file's gallery offers, as core lists the classes a MAT-file can hold, or
null, the default, for a dictionary's gallery, which offers every tile. The gallery draws the
tiles of these classes only (the model's matCatalog). Property only.

members.name: addSections
members.description:
With `addClasses`, the sections beside the file's variables whose every tile its gallery
offers too, each tile naming its section: a model's configuration sets, `config`. Null, the
default: none. Property only.

members.name: rowDrag
members.description:
Whether a row can be dragged, or a dragged row let go over one. Set it false where the
document cannot be changed: no row is draggable, and a drag from another table draws no drop
target here, on a row or on the empty body. Default true. Attribute `row-drag`.

members.name: readonly
members.description:
A viewer: the user selects, opens, searches, sorts, filters and copies, and changes nothing.
No cell editor opens — not on a double-click, not on Enter, not for beginRename or
openWholeValueEditor — and no cell is drawn as editable; the `+ Add` button is not drawn
whatever canAdd says, and no row is dragged or takes a drop whatever rowDrag says. So none of
the events those gestures send (dex-edit-completed, dex-edit-text-request, dex-add-entry,
dex-row-drag-start, dex-row-drop) is sent. A right-click still sends dex-table-context-menu:
what a read-only menu offers is the app's to say (buildContextMenuItems with editable false).
False, the default, is the table as it always was, each cell's own flags deciding. Reflected
to the attribute `readonly`.

members.name: keyboardMenu
members.description:
Whether Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key, pressed on the grid, open the row menu: they send
`dex-table-context-menu` for the keyboard's current row (the row the arrows last moved to, else
the selection's last, whichever the table shows), placed under that row as a right-click on it
is, with `keyboard: true` (connectTable then gives the menu the keyboard); with no such row, for
the space under the rows. Both keys are spent, so the browser's own menu event for them does
not follow, and the grid names them (`aria-keyshortcuts`). A field's keys stay the field's (a
cell editor, a header's filter button). False, the default, leaves both keys to the browser, as
they always were. Attribute `keyboard-menu`.

members.name: storageKey
members.description:
Where the user's column choices (which are shown, and their order) are kept: the page's
localStorage, under `<storageKey>-column-order`, `<storageKey>-hidden-columns` and
`<storageKey>-known-columns`. The default, 'dex', is the keys every table has always used,
so a layout saved before this existed carries over — and every table on the page that keeps
the default shares one layout. An app gives each kind of table a key of its own, or null
(or '') to keep the choices for this element's life only, with localStorage never touched.
They are read when the table is connected, so set it before the table goes into the page: a
key set later reads them again, from that key, after the table has shown the ones under the
key it had. Attribute `storage-key`.

members.name: selectedRowId
members.description:
The last of `selectedRowIds`, or '' when nothing is selected; set, it selects that row alone
('' selects nothing). Sends nothing.

members.name: expandedIds
members.description:
The rows shown open, by id: a copy, the caller's to keep.

Set it to open exactly these rows — an expansion the app saved, or the one it read before
giving the table new rows (nextExpandedIds keeps those that still exist). An id with no row is
kept, and opens its row if one comes. Setting it fetches nothing; expand() is the twisty's
click, which asks for children the payload held back.

members.name: expand
members.description:
Opens these rows as a click on each one's twisty does: a row with nothing under it stays
closed, and a row whose children the payload held back (`_lazy`) asks for them once
(dex-request-children). Read off `rows` as they are now, so it may follow an assignment of
them directly.

members.name: collapse
members.description: Closes these rows.

members.name: expandTopLevel
members.description:
The expansion an app otherwise keeps around every assignment of `rows`, kept by the table
(nextExpandedIds): the first rows with any in them open their top level — a dictionary's
sections, a MAT-file's variables, though not one whose children were held back, whose first
click fetches — and from then on the rows the user opened stay open while they exist, and
what they closed stays closed. Off, the default, a change of `rows` leaves the expansion as it
was, to the app (expandedIds). Attribute `expand-top-level`.

members.name: dropPredictor

type.text:
| ((
        targetRowId: string,
        mode: 'copy' | 'move',
      ) => { canDrop: boolean; cursor: string; tooltip: string; noop: boolean } | null)
    | null

members.description:
Predicts a drop for the row under the cursor ('' for the space under the rows), as the
dragover goes: whether it may drop, the cursor and the tooltip to show, and whether it would
change nothing. The app sets it, from the model's dropDecision and what it knows is being
dragged (a drag can come from another table). Returns null when it cannot predict — no drag
it was told about, or a target with no rule — and null REFUSES: with a predictor, "cannot
say" is not "yes". With none, the default, any row takes a drop and the space under the rows
takes none. Property only.

members.name: toggleAddGallery
members.description:
Opens the `+ Add` gallery under the Add button, or closes it if it is open, as a click on the
button does: an app's keyboard shortcut for adding an entry. It opens nothing while the button
is not drawn (`canAdd` false, or `readonly`).

members.name: beginRename
members.description:
Opens the Name editor on a row, as a double-click on its Name does: what an app calls after
adding an entry the user should name (`dex-add-entry`'s `rename`). The edit comes back as
`dex-edit-completed`. Returns whether the editor opened: false when the row is not in `rows`
yet, so an app can call again once it is, or when its Name cannot be edited.

members.name: openWholeValueEditor
members.description:
The answer to `dex-edit-text-request`: opens the Value editor of `rowId` on `text`, the whole
value the cell's summary stands for. In a textarea, as the text can be one long line of up to
200,000 characters; committed unchanged it sends nothing, and changed it sends
`dex-edit-completed` with the whole text. Only the answer to the last request opens an
editor, and only while no other editor is open and the cell still takes this one: an answer
that arrives after the user moved on opens nothing.

members.name: commitEdit
members.description:
Commits the cell editor open now, if any, as Enter would: its edit comes back as
`dex-edit-completed` when the text changed, and the keyboard goes back to the table. Returns
whether an editor was open. For a host that saves or closes the document while an edit is still
being typed.

members.name: focusFilter
members.description: Focuses (and selects) the search input: an app's Ctrl+F.

members.name: flashRow
members.description: Flashes a row's background once, on the next render, as a copy does; nothing if it is not drawn.

events.name: dex-add-entry
events.description: A tile of the `+ Add` gallery was clicked: add one entry of that class, renaming it if `rename`.

events.name: dex-request-children
events.description:
A row whose children the payload held back (`_lazy`) was opened: answer with its rows,
merged into `rows` under it (connectTable asks its source's `children` and merges them in
place). Asked once until its rows arrive.

events.name: dex-table-context-menu
events.description:
A right-click on a row (after selecting it) or on the space under the rows, or with
`keyboardMenu` Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key on the grid, for the keyboard's row: open a
context menu there.

events.name: dex-row-selected
events.description:
The user changed the selection: a click, Ctrl/Cmd- or Shift-click, a key, select-all, or a
right-click on a row not in it.

events.name: dex-row-drag-start
events.description: The user started dragging rows.

events.name: dex-row-drag-end
events.description: A drag of this table's rows ended, dropped or not. No detail.

events.name: dex-row-drop
events.description:
Rows were let go over a row the dropPredictor accepts (any row, with no predictor), or over
the space under the rows when it accepts that.

events.name: dex-edit-text-request
events.description: A Value editor is opening on a summary: send the whole text with openWholeValueEditor.

events.name: dex-edit-completed
events.description: A cell edit was committed with a text that differs from the one it had.

events.name: dex-link-clicked
events.description:
A link in a cell was clicked: a Data Type, Used By, a block or a parameter. `target` says
what it points at; see LinkClickedDetail for its forms.

declarations.name: defineTreeTable
declarations.description:
Registers the widget as `<dex-tree-table>`, or under `tag`, after the parts its template draws,
which keep their default names: the + Add gallery, the column-filter popup, the filter bar, the
icon and the matrix glyph. Parts first, so a part whose name is taken throws before the table
is registered at all.

declarations.name: isTypingInField
declarations.description: Whether `ev` is typing in a field of the table's (its search box, a column filter, a cell editor) rather than a gesture on the grid.

declarations.name: wireEditing
declarations.description: Wire the editing half: the listeners go on through `host.listen`, the state stays in here.

declarations.name: shouldShowContextMenu
declarations.description:
Whether a right-click should open the context menu at all. Read-only
documents get NO menu — the read-only byte-backed view has no copy/paste/
mutation handlers, so an all-disabled menu would be dead UI.

declarations.name: shouldOpenCellEditor
declarations.description:
Whether a double-click / Enter should open the inline cell editor. Gated on
the document-level flag only: read-only documents never open the editor,
regardless of any per-row `editable` flag (which is a coloring signal).

declarations.name: buildContextMenuItems
declarations.description:
Build the right-click context menu for the CURRENT SELECTION.

Pure and synchronous: enablement comes from the host-computed row flags, the cached
clipboard state, the target section's rules, whether the document is editable, and where its
undo stack stands when the source says — no round-trip. Two things it deliberately does NOT decide: which rows are operands
(resolveOperands does, so the keyboard cannot diverge) and whether a payload may land
in a section (dropDecision.rejectReason does, so a Paste offered here is a drop the
hover feedback would allow).

GROUPS, THEN JOIN. The items are built as groups and the separators are put between
whatever groups survive. A section header's menu — Paste, then Undo/Redo — then falls
out of dropping the two empty groups, with no case of its own; so does the binary
format's missing "Location in Text". Managing separators by hand is how a menu ends
up with two in a row or one at the bottom, and that is exactly what this shape makes
impossible.

A matrix's cells as a read-only grid, one page at a time, headed by MATLAB's 1-based row and
column numbers, with a page selector over the dimensions past the second. Only the cells near
the scroll position are built, so a 1000x1000 page scrolls as a small one does. The arrow
keys, Home and End move between cells and PageUp and PageDown between pages; a cell whose text
is clipped shows it whole as its tooltip. Escape is left to the panel around it.
`<dex-variable-editor>` draws it.
declarations.name: DexMatrixGrid

members.name: matrix
members.description: The matrix shown, cells included; null, the default, draws nothing. Property only.

members.name: pageCount
members.description: How many pages the matrix has: the product of its dimensions past the second, 1 for 2-D.

members.name: page
members.description: The page shown, from 0; set, it is clamped to the pages there are.

members.name: pageLabel
members.description: A page's subscript as MATLAB writes it, `(:,:,2)` or `(:,:,1,3)`; '' for a 2-D matrix.

members.name: cellText
members.description: The text of cell (`r`, `c`), from 0, of a page (the one shown by default); '' outside the matrix.

members.name: focusActiveCell
members.description: Focuses the cell the keyboard is on, (1,1) until it has moved.

cssProperties.name: --dex-matrix-max-height
cssProperties.description: The largest the variable editor's grid grows before it scrolls.

declarations.name: defineMatrixGrid
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-matrix-grid>`, or under `tag`.

The variable editor: a panel, anchored under the glyph that opened it, that shows a matrix's
cells in a `<dex-matrix-grid>`. An app makes one and appends it to the page; show() opens it
on a matrix's descriptor, with its title and a waiting line, and deliver() fills it in with
the cells once the app has them. Escape, the close button, a click outside it or a scroll
close it, and focus goes back to the glyph if the panel held it. It sends no events.
declarations.name: DexVariableEditor

members.name: show
members.description:
Opens the panel under `anchorEl` (the glyph, which gets focus back) on what the row knew:
name, class, shape, node id. The cells are not here yet — the app fetches them for
`matrix.nodeId` (the model's matrixCellsMessage builds the answer) and hands it to
deliver(). Until then the panel shows its title and a waiting line.

members.name: deliver
members.description:
The cells the app fetched for the panel show() opened: fills the panel in, or says why it
cannot be filled in (the answer's `message`). Ignores an answer that is not about what is
currently on screen: open A, change your mind, open B, and A's reply can still be in flight —
taking it would put A's numbers under B's title, which is worse than a slow panel.

members.name: close
members.description: Closes the panel; focus goes back to the glyph that opened it, if the panel held it.

members.name: reposition
members.description:
Places the panel again under its glyph, left edges aligned, pulled in at the viewport's
edges and flipped above the glyph when there is no room below. show() and deliver() call it.

declarations.name: defineVariableEditor
declarations.description: Registers the widget as `<dex-variable-editor>`, or under `tag`, after the grid it shows.
